--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.katz_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Get Katz centrality for each node. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.katz_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Get Katz centrality for each node. title: >- [Graph.katz_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get Katz centrality for each node. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get Katz centrality for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L62424-L62656){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.katz_centrality( alpha=0.1, beta=1.0, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, normalized=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Katz centrality](../assets/graphs/katz-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same five-node directed graph shaded by Katz centrality with alpha 0.5, which counts incoming walks. D receives walks from A, B and C and scores 0.32, E, fed through D, 0.26, B and C 0.16, and the source A, which nothing reaches, 0.11." width="100%"} Katz centrality measures node influence based on the number of walks of all lengths reaching the node, with walks weighted by `α^length`: `x = α · Aᵀ · x + β` where α is the attenuation factor, `Aᵀ` is the transpose of the adjacency matrix, and `β` is a bias vector: by default the same baseline for every node, but `beta=` can also give each node its own. For directed graphs, this counts incoming paths, making it suitable for measuring "prestige" or "influence received". Key differences from other centralities: - PageRank: uses teleportation and out-degree normalization - Eigenvector: only considers infinite-length walks (principal eigenvector) - Alpha centrality: uses `A` instead of `Aᵀ` (outgoing vs incoming) - Katz: weights walks by path length, considers all finite walks Because every node receives the same baseline `β`, nodes that nothing points to still get a non-zero score, which makes Katz centrality well behaved on directed acyclic graphs where eigenvector centrality degenerates. Typical uses include: - ranking papers, patents, or packages by direct and indirect citations or dependencies - measuring prestige in follower or endorsement networks - scoring nodes when short chains of influence should count more than long ones The scores are found by fixed-point iteration starting from `β`, then (by default) rescaled to sum to `1`. Edge weights are ignored. For undirected graphs `Aᵀ = A`, so with the default `beta=` the result is identical to `alpha_centrality()` with the same `alpha=`. If `alpha=` is at or above `1 / λ_max` the iteration diverges and a `RuntimeWarning` is emitted (the scores are then meaningless), so keep `alpha=` comfortably small. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Attenuation factor for walk lengths. Must be smaller than the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue (typically < `0.2` for safety). Higher values give more weight to longer paths. Defaults to `0.1`. For a directed acyclic graph the largest eigenvalue is `0`, so any positive value converges. [beta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | dict[int | str, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Baseline score each node contributes, as a single number for all nodes (default `1.0`) or as a dictionary mapping every node (by ID or label) to its own baseline. Per-node baselines let some nodes matter more as sources of influence, for example to weight citations by the citing paper's venue. A single number only scales the raw scores, so with the default `normalized=True` every positive value gives the same result; it matters with `normalized=False`. A dictionary that leaves out a node raises a `ValueError`. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations. Defaults to `100`. If the scores have not converged by then, the values from the last iteration are returned and a `RuntimeWarning` is emitted. Convergence slows as `alpha=` approaches `1 / λ_max`. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence threshold. Iteration stops once the largest absolute change of any node's (unnormalized) score between two iterations falls below `tol=`. Defaults to `1e-6`. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name used to store the scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), the column is named `"katz_centrality"`. An existing column with the same name is overwritten. Only used when `return_dict=` is `False`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the scores as a dictionary and leave the node DataFrame untouched. If `False` (default), store the scores under `attr_name=` and return the graph for method chaining. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), rescale the scores to sum to `1` so they can be compared across graphs. If `False`, return the raw solution of `x = α · Aᵀ · x + β`, whose scale follows `beta=` (this matches NetworkX's `normalized=False`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to Katz centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. With the default `normalized=True` the scores sum to `1.0`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Katz centrality (Katz, 1953) generalizes eigenvector centrality by giving every node a baseline contribution and geometrically discounting influence with distance. The iteration converges to the closed-form solution $c = (I - \alpha A^\top)^{-1} \beta$ (with $\beta$ the vector of baselines, $\beta \mathbf{1}$ for a single number), which exists only when $\alpha < 1/\lambda_{\max}(A)$; sensible defaults sit around $\alpha \approx 0.1$ and rarely above $0.2$. For directed graphs the transpose matters: high Katz signals prestige (many incoming paths, weighted toward short ones), while for undirected graphs $A^\top = A$ and the metric coincides with alpha centrality. Final scores are normalized to sum to $1$ by default so they can be compared across graphs of different sizes; this also means a constant $\beta$ cancels out of the result, while a per-node $\beta$ (or `normalized=False`) does not. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~eigen_centrality`) : The limit as the decay approaches its maximum. [](`~alpha_centrality`) : A version with a baseline status per node. [](`~pagerank`) : A random walk with teleportation. ## Examples {.doc-examples} "D" receives edges both directly from "A" and by way of "B" and "C", so it has the highest Katz score, while "A", which nothing points to, has only the baseline and scores lowest: ::: {#ae9f26fc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("A", "D")], directed=True ) graph.katz_centrality().get_node_df().select("label", "katz_centrality") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Between degree and eigenvector Katz counts the walks that end at a node, each one discounted by `alpha=` per step. With a small `alpha=` only the shortest walks count and the ranking is close to degree's; near the limit of `1 / lambda_max` (the largest adjacency eigenvalue), long walks count too and it approaches `eigen_centrality()`. In *Les Misérables* the limit is `1 / 12`, so the default `alpha=0.1` diverges (with a `RuntimeWarning`). Here are the places at `alpha=0.01` and at `alpha=0.08`, which needs more iterations to converge: ::: {#1773f8bc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl lesmis = ( ec.les_miserables() .katz_centrality(alpha=0.01, attr_name="short") .katz_centrality(alpha=0.08, max_iter=1000, attr_name="long") ) places = lesmis.get_node_df().with_columns( pl.col("short", "long").rank("min", descending=True).cast(pl.Int64) ) places.select("label", "degree", "short", "long").sort("short").head(8) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

Coloring each character by the places gained (or, below zero, lost) shows where the climbers are: ::: {#3b8b42f7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} climb = dict(zip(places["label"], places["short"] - places["long"])) lesmis.set_node_attrs("climb", climb).plot( color_by="climb", color_scale="diverging", size_by="long", label_by="label", seed=3, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Directed acyclic graphs In a graph with no cycles, every walk ends, so the scores converge for any `alpha=`; `eigen_centrality()` doesn't converge on one at all. In the `citations()` network, Katz counts the chains of citations leading to each paper, and with `alpha=0.5` the seminal Moreau 2000 has more than twice the score of any other paper: ::: {#25b569fd .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} citations = ec.citations().katz_centrality(alpha=0.5) citations.plot(layout="pos", color_by="katz_centrality", label_by="label") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: To give some nodes a higher baseline than others, pass `beta=` as a dictionary.
